sol.section: §9.2 budget-table identity matching; §7.3 oracle identity; §16.2 wrapper prologue; §19.9 resolved build record
sol.problem:
§9.2 says “An entry matches a region by its identity (§7.3, the interface hash of @ref of one shape)” and “For each component a region takes, in order of precedence, the first entry matching by identity”. That includes sstack. §16.2 then emits the shadow-stack setup with “c = lift.const.i64 <sstack>”. This makes the selector depend on the value it selects, and no provisional identity, staging rule or other default breaks the cycle. Witness: use the supported O0 pipeline on `define i8 @f(i8 %x) { %p = alloca [24 x i8], align 8
 store i8 %x, ptr %p, align 1
 %v = load i8, ptr %p, align 1
 ret i8 %v
 }`, an IN(8,zext)/tgt=8 shape, a fixed runtime/link layout and adequate other budgets. LLVM 18 and 23 both verify it and retain the alloca/load under default<O0>. Let H16 and H32 be the interface hashes of its canonical reference objects using sstack=16 and 32 respectively, with all other inputs and raw-table maxima fixed. Use table `{"version":"0.2","defaults":{"steps":"1048576","heap":"1048576","stack":"65536","depth":"256","sstack":"16"},"entries":[{"identity":"H16","sstack":"32"}]}`, substituting the actual H16 digest. If the final object is H16, the entry matches and requires sstack=32, changing the object to H32. If it is H32, the entry does not match and requires the default 16. Thus the literal final-identity rule has no fixed point; a one-pass implementation and a rematching implementation cannot follow one common specified construction. This is semantic configuration, not a field-format omission: with initially unset stack state and helpers needing no additional shadow frames on this path, 16 cannot admit f’s 24-byte frame, whereas 32 can. Independently, hashing the existing entry-stack microvector through bennett-isa-ref hash /dev/stdin confirms the hash dependence: its original init-size constant 16 gives ref hash 50289e34598400f57c820d819d83993e14d12e08596ba55ce070109b5746ad1f; changing only that wrapper constant to 32 gives 100b604880ad883157e645eb234be2edfb5897d851f73321d554915b8d14509c. This microvector probe establishes hash sensitivity, not a claim that it is f’s canonical object.
sol.fix: Replace the identity-matching/precedence paragraph of §9.2 with this ordered rule, and cross-reference it from §7.3, §16.2 and §19.9: “Budget-table resolution is staged and does not seek a fixed point. First resolve baseline values for every region and component using the first matching region_key entry, then the first matching symbol entry, then the defaults, ignoring identity entries. Freeze the link’s layout capacities using the componentwise maxima of all defaults, table entries and statically supplied budget records, whether an entry matches or not; later lookup does not shrink or recompute those capacities. Construct each shape’s provisional reference object under that layout using its baseline sstack and other baseline wrapper inputs. Its interface hash is selection_identity. For each component, overlay the first identity entry naming that component whose identity equals selection_identity, or retain the baseline value if none matches. Apply this overlay once only. Generate the final reference object using the resolved values; its interface hash remains the semantic identity of §7.3. Do not re-evaluate identity selectors against that final hash. Record selection_identity, final semantic identity and resolved components in the build record and resolved budget table.” Existing explicit marker-record/table-sentinel precedence remains in force. Add the witness above to DD/DM: an entry keyed by H16 selects 32 exactly once, the final wrapper contains the size constant 32 and has H32, and its build record retains selection_identity=H16. Also test that changing only steps preserves the final object hash while changing the selected token. Another viable repair is a separately defined content hash of the pre-budget closure/shape with symbolic wrapper/layout inputs, used solely for budget lookup; specify its canonical construction and keep final ISA identity separate. I recommend the staged provisional-object rule because it reuses ISA hashing, preserves identity-based configuration and requires no new hash encoding. Removing identity selectors or silently ignoring identity-selected sstack would lose the advertised capability and is not the proposed repair.

codex.fix:
Replace the offset-computation portion of §5.2 PT2 with:
"PT2 uses the pointer address space’s P(a) and I(a), and the complete finite-width GEP semantics of §16.4, also for constant expressions. Sequential indices are sign-extended or truncated to I(a), scaling and offset accumulation are modulo 2^I(a), and addition preserves the pointer bits above I(a). A statically zero accumulated offset copies AV(p) unchanged. Unbounded mathematical addition of object offsets must not substitute for this computation. For every represented (X,o), the abstract result includes the image of all represented addresses and index values under that finite-width computation; unknown base bits range over the patterns consistent with DataLayout and the object’s alignment. Represent the resulting offset union using the existing integer/residue-class/* domain. If an address may leave X, include (EXT,*) and the non-handle top flag instead of dropping that address. PT6 propagates that unknown-address alternative; ROOT provenance and §6.2’s restrictions remain explicit. Array dimensions determine stride, never an index bound."
Keep §§16.4 and 17.4’s corrected concrete GEP rows. Add a recognition/execution witness using the module above: AV(%p)={(tab,0)}, AV(%f)={FN(body)}, candidates={body}, verdict=accept and no T-REGION/fault. Check both the supported O0 form and the instcombine form. The abstract-offset rule must agree with the concrete map before dispatch domains are frozen.

codex.problem:
PT5 says "a range(lo, hi) attribute or !range metadata (read before N3 removes it) restricts ⊤ to [lo, hi)". N4 then removes range attributes, and §§12.1/18.1 define execution on that materialised module. The old range is therefore not necessarily a bound on the program whose values dispatch must handle. Witness, verified and retained by LLVM 23 default<O0>:
 declare ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64, i64)
 declare void @__bennett_gate(i32, ptr, i64)
 declare void @__bennett_qfree(ptr)
 define void @top(i64 range(i64 1, 2) %n) {
   %m = and i64 %n, 3
   %w = or i64 %m, 1
   %h = call ptr @__bennett_qalloc(i64 0, i64 %w)
   call void @__bennett_gate(i32 1, ptr %h, i64 2)
   call void @__bennett_gate(i32 1, ptr %h, i64 2)
   call void @__bennett_qfree(ptr %h)
   ret void
 }
PT5 gives VS(%w)={1}, reproduced by the recogniser with verdict accept. After N4, the entry has no range precondition: n=2 computes w=3, both X gates on wire 2 succeed and the register is freed cleanly. Re-analysing the actual materialised module gives {1,3}, also reproduced, and LLVM 18/23 fold its arithmetic probe at n=2 to 3. A plugin retaining the specified pre-N4 domain has only the width-1 alternative and faults or allocates the wrong width. This is not a claim about executing the original ranged function outside its precondition: the counterexample is to the explicitly defined, annotation-free materialised program and §18.7’s all-host-input conformance requirement. No optimiser erased this execution in the O0 witness.
codex.fix:
Replace the final clause of PT5 with:
"A range attribute or !range metadata that N3 or N4 removes is not a reference bound on materialised execution. It must not restrict a value set used for a verdict, candidate set, descriptor shape or dispatch domain. A range independently established by the materialised instructions may restrict the set; otherwise retain top and apply the ordinary operation rules, including the finite mask/remainder rules."
In N3 delete "after §5 has read !range, PT5" and state: "N3/N4-removed range information is ignored when computing the §5 reference domains." In §3.4’s finite-width examples replace "range attributes and metadata" with "bounds established by materialised instructions".
For the witness require VS(%w)={1,3}, verdict=accept and, at n=2, width=3, two successful X gates on wire 2, clean free and fault code 0. Add the parameter-attribute witness on LLVM 23 and an equivalent load-!range witness on LLVM 18/23. Two viable implementations are to ignore these annotations in S2 or to compute S2 on a virtual N3/N4-stripped view; I recommend the stripped view, preserving the single reference fixpoint. Keeping the annotations as new runtime preconditions would change the materialised semantics and is not the repair.

Add this explicit exception to §12.2 N9, before the common store and old-result substitution:
"For atomicrmw nand ptr p, iW v, after %nz.l.r = load iW, ptr p emit %nz.a.r = and iW %nz.l.r, v, then %nz.v.r = xor iW %nz.a.r, -1, with no overflow flags. Store %nz.v.r to p and replace every use of the atomicrmw result by %nz.l.r. These two logical instructions, in this order, are the canonical expansion."
Add a normalise/native witness with the source above and the output load/and/xor/store/load/ret sequence; require old=240, new=63 and code=0 on LLVM 18 and 23. A De Morgan expansion (xor each operand with all ones, then or) is also value-correct but has a different reference cost; select the two-operation and/xor expansion above and pin its mapped step count. No new rejection or ISA blocker is needed.
